findings_qualitative.value: Gravitational infall causes a rapid increase in optically thin line width toward the core center, whereas homogeneous turbulent line broadening decreases slightly only at the core edge and remains nearly flat toward the center.

evidence.quote: In particular, gravitational infall motion would give rise to a rapid increase of line width toward the core center, whereas the contribution from turbulence remains almost invariant with decreasing radius.

findings_qualitative.value: OMC3-mms7 has initiated gravitational collapse, whereas OMC3-m is turbulence-dominated and in hydrostatic balance.

evidence.quote: For OMC3-mms7, we find that CI is much larger than 0.3, suggesting that gravitational collapse has already initiated in this core.
On the other hand, the CI of OMC3-m is close to 0.3, indicating that its non-thermal line width is dominated by turbulence, and the core has not started to collapse.

findings_qualitative.value: Three isolated low-mass starless cores (L183, L1498, L1517B) all have CI significantly smaller than 0.3, indicating they are in hydrostatic balance and not undergoing global free-fall collapse.

evidence.quote: The CI for all these isolated starless cores is found to be significantly smaller than 0.3, suggesting that they are not collapsing (cf. Fig. [3](#fig:2panel_core)).

findings_qualitative.value: Non-thermal turbulent velocity dispersions in all five studied cores (both OMC and isolated low-mass cores) are subsonic.

evidence.quote: The velocity dispersions in all the cores are subsonic, which validates our theoretical treatment based on the scaling behavior of incompressible or weakly compressible turbulence.

claims.hypothesis: The radial profile of the non-thermal line width of an optically thin molecular tracer (quantified by the Collapsing Index, CI) can distinguish between a gravitationally collapsing core (CI >> 0.3) and a hydrostatic, turbulence-supported core (CI <= 0.3).
claims.experiment: Derived analytical predictions for line-of-sight velocity dispersion from Kolmogorov turbulence (CI = 0.3) and singular isothermal sphere infall (CI = 5.3), and applied the CI metric and radial profile model fitting to ALMA+Nobeyama N2H+ (J=1-0) maps of OMC3-mms7 and OMC3-m.
claims.result: Measured CI = 1.90 (v_g(R) = 0.16 km/s, u_t(R) = 0.12 km/s) for OMC3-mms7 and CI = 0.32 (v_g(R) = 0.03 km/s, u_t(R) = 0.27 km/s) for OMC3-m; corroborated by asymmetric 13CO/C18O blue profiles in OMC3-mms7 and symmetric profiles in OMC3-m.
claims.finding: OMC3-mms7 is undergoing gravitational collapse while OMC3-m is in hydrostatic equilibrium, demonstrating that CI effectively diagnoses the dynamical status of dense cores.

evidence.quote: Inserting Equation [\[equ:utinter\]](#equ:utinter) and [\[equ:vginter\]](#equ:vginter) into the definition of the index gives CI = 0.3 and 5.3, respectively.
A calculation using the observed $\sigma_{m NT}$ for the selected Orion cores shows that CI = 1.90 and 0.32 for OMC3-mms7 and OMC3-m, respectively.
For OMC3-mms7, the gravitational collapse velocity is slightly larger than the turbulent velocity even at the edge of the core, suggesting that it is already undergoing gravitational collapse.

claims.hypothesis: Isolated low-mass starless cores L183, L1498, and L1517B are in hydrostatic balance rather than advanced gravitational collapse.
claims.experiment: Calculated the Collapsing Index (CI) and normalized non-thermal velocity dispersion radial profiles for L183, L1498, and L1517B using literature single-dish N2H+ (J=1-0) line width maps and NH3 kinetic temperatures.
claims.result: All three isolated cores exhibit CI values significantly smaller than 0.3 and subsonic non-thermal velocity dispersions.
claims.finding: All three isolated low-mass cores are in hydrostatic balance; the CI method does not classify small-amplitude initial contraction or envelope expansion with core collapse (EECC) motions as core collapse.

evidence.quote: The CI for all these isolated starless cores is found to be significantly smaller than 0.3, suggesting that they are not collapsing (cf. Fig. [3](#fig:2panel_core)).
Our CI method, as shown in Fig. [3](#fig:2panel_core), does not identify these possible initial stage, small amplitude core contracting motion or EECC motion as core collapse.

why_this_data.value: ALMA combined with Nobeyama provides high spatial resolution (~3" or 0.006 pc, smaller than the ~0.01 pc thermal Jeans scale) and high sensitivity (~12 mJy/beam, >2x deeper than Hacar et al. 2018) in N2H+ (J=1-0), an optically thin and chemically stable tracer that probes deep into dense cores.

evidence.loc: Collapsing Index: A New Method to Identify Star-forming Cores Based on ALMA Images
evidence.quote: A meaningful measurement of CI requires spatially and spectrally resolved images of optically thin and chemically stable dense gas tracers.
The spatial resolution is $\sim$3", corresponding to 0.006 pc, smaller than the thermal Jeans scale $\sim 0.01$ pc; the rms noise is $\sim$12 mJy/beam, and the velocity resolution is 0.11 km/s.
For the cores selected for this study, our data are more than 2 times deeper compared to (cite: hacar2018) of 25 mJy/beam, thus provide better dynamic range.

why_this_method.value: Canonical column density radial profile methods suffer from projection effects and resolution limits, whereas turbulent motions and gravitational infall have distinct spatial line-width behaviors along the radius of a core.

evidence.quote: However, due to the projection effect and the resolution limit, the observed column density profile can hardly distinguish different theoretical models unambiguously

In particular, gravitational infall motion would give rise to a rapid increase of line width toward the core center, whereas the contribution from turbulence remains almost invariant with decreasing radius.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Including core rotation and bipolar outflows in the line-width model was rejected because adding at least three more parameters (scaling, radial distribution of rotation velocity, inclination angle) would smear the distinct signatures of gravity and turbulence.

evidence.quote: If rotation is considered, at least three more parameters, i.e. the scaling and radial distribution of the rotation velocity, and the inclination angle of the rotation axis have to be added in the model.
The increase of complication will smear the different features of gravity and turbulence found in this paper.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using density-weighted integration of the infall velocity dispersion (Equation B.7) was tested and rejected in favor of the unweighted analytical approximation (Equation 4) because both give qualitatively very similar radial profiles.

limitations_admitted.value: The speculation that collapse-induced turbulent velocity scales as r^-1/2 is based on dimensional analysis and needs to be tested by future numerical simulations.

evidence.quote: Our speculation is subject to tests by future numerical simulations of turbulence in a collapsing core.

limitations_admitted.value: The CI method does not detect very initial stage, small-amplitude contracting motions or envelope expansion with core collapse (EECC) motions.

evidence.quote: Our CI method, as shown in Fig. [3](#fig:2panel_core), does not identify these possible initial stage, small amplitude core contracting motion or EECC motion as core collapse.

limitations_admitted.value: The method is currently restricted to approximately spherical cores with negligible rotation and minimal influence from bipolar outflows.

evidence.quote: We have restricted our study to a selection of prestellar cores with spherical morphology that are not significantly affected by rotation or bipolar outflows.

referee_caveats_inferred: The analytical model assumes uniform weighting along the line of sight in the main text; while Appendix A shows density weighting (rho^2) gives a qualitatively similar curve, the exact value of the critical CI threshold and fitted v_g(R) could shift quantitatively under realistic density and abundance profiles.

N2H+ (J=1-0) has hyperfine structure; the paper mentions using SCOUSE (a multi-Gaussian fitter) rather than an explicit hyperfine-structure fitting routine, without specifying how the 7 hyperfine components or optical depth were handled when extracting the intrinsic line width.

OMC3-mms7 is associated with a known bipolar outflow ~10" north of the core center; although argued to be on the periphery, outflow-driven shocks or unresolved velocity gradients could still contaminate the central line width.
Uncertainties on the fitted parameters u_t(R) and v_g(R) and on the measured CI values are not reported.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~1-10 GB (single ALMA Band 3 spectral line mosaic project 2013.1.00662.S combined with Nobeyama single-dish data)
reproducibility.score_reason: The mathematical formulation of the Collapsing Index and the fitting equations are completely and transparently derived, and key intermediate parameters (core radii, kinetic temperatures, threshold radii) are explicitly stated. However, full reproduction from raw archive data is blocked because the ALMA+Nobeyama data combination is deferred to a companion paper (Yue et al. 2020), the exact coordinates of the two selected cores (particularly 'OMC3-m') are omitted, and the treatment of N2H+ hyperfine structure in SCOUSE is not specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Although the main results are clean numeric values (CI, u_t, v_g), reproducing them requires the combined ALMA+Nobeyama N2H+ cube from Yue et al. (2020) and the exact sky coordinates of 'OMC3-m' and 'OMC3-mms7', neither of which is explicitly provided in this paper.

methods_papers.why: SCOUSE multi-Gaussian spectral line fitting engine used to fit N2H+ line profiles
mpfit non-linear least-squares fitting algorithm used to fit the radial profile of non-thermal velocity dispersion
Analytical recipe for deprojecting observed core axis ratios and correcting gravitational potential energy for ellipsoidal morphology
Method used to analyze core rotation and calculate specific angular momentum

companion_papers.why: Companion paper presenting the combined ALMA and Nobeyama N2H+ (J=1-0) observations and data reduction of the OMC 2/3 region
